title: Baseline SII and SIRI identify immune-inflammatory susceptibility and improve risk stratification of early subclinical cardiac dysfunction during non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor therapy
summary: In a single-center cohort of 269 postmenopausal patients, 63 met the study-defined cardiac dysfunction endpoint. Adding SII or SIRI improved internal AUC from 0.633 to 0.745 or 0.733, respectively; both markers were independently associated with the endpoint. The paper reports covariate-adjusted regression, sensitivity analyses, five-fold cross-validation with fold-wise preprocessing, and calibration/decision analyses. Small cohort, 63 events, retrospective operational endpoint, residual selection bias, and no external validation prevent claims of clinical implementation or validated prediction.
ai_technology: Baseline SII/SIRI were evaluated in logistic prediction models with stratified five-fold out-of-fold predictions; an exploratory machine-learning analysis also used an SVM to classify overlapping endpoint components.
organization: Department of Cardiology, First Affiliated Hospital of Xi’an Jiaotong University, Xi’an, China
